asks: Keep Strathcona-Sherwood Park near its current boundaries: do not add half of Beaumont or move Heritage Hills out; if population must be added, take Tofield, and give Sherwood Park Strathcona County north of Highway 16 up to Highway 15.

Keep the interim St. Albert and St. Albert-Sturgeon boundaries as they are, with Boudreau Road as the divide, and do not move the Woodlands neighbourhood (polls 43 to 45) from St. Albert-Sturgeon into St. Albert.

quote: I hope that the commission will continue to maintain the status quo in both St. Albert ridings and avoid any further changes.
note: Supports the interim pattern (one urban St. Albert riding, one St. Albert-Sturgeon hybrid). Rejects a specific S4 proposal from written submissions: moving Woodlands (polls 43, 44, 45) out of St. Albert-Sturgeon into St. Albert: 'this would be a poor decision because it would reduce effective representation' (EB-776). needs_geometry because whether either final map moves Woodlands depends on the lines.

quote: The approach used in St. Albert, one fully urban riding and one hybrid riding, should be used in other small cities with a similar population like Medicine Hat or Airdrie.
note: Recommends the St. Albert model (one all-urban riding, one city-rural hybrid) for Airdrie as a general idea; no option in the table matches (A1 makes both Airdrie seats hybrids). Passing remark in a St. Albert presentation.

asks: No change requested; she is satisfied with the interim report but remains skeptical of pairing Calgary or Edmonton with areas outside their boundaries and of reducing Edmonton's downtown ridings.

note: Lethbridge appears only inside a passage she reads from the interim report about a southern Alberta presenter; she takes no stance on Lethbridge. Her hybrid skepticism is about Calgary and Edmonton.

asks: Do not divide Clearwater County and western Mountain View County three ways; create a Banff-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre west-central riding along Highway 22 and Highway 11 reaching to the BC border with the back of Banff National Park and the Big Horn, O'Chiese and Sunchild reserves, with Cremona on the Highway 22 side and Canmore-Kananaskis kept separate.

quote: I will conclude, though, with an alternative proposal for a BanffRocky Mountain House-Sundre riding.
note: Rejects interim three-way split: 'I'm here to share my community's concerns with the proposed dissolution of western Mountain View county and Clearwater county into three different ridings' (EB-780). Wants Clearwater County, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre, Caroline and western Mountain View County together along Highway 22; agrees Rimbey and Ponoka go elsewhere and with the interim Lacombe changes.

quote: the extensive historical precedent for maintaining a west-central riding that encompasses Clearwater county, western Mountain View county, all the way to the B.C. border.
note: Proposes a Banff-Rocky Mountain House-Sundre riding including the back country of Banff National Park ('isolating the national parks from the rest of west-central Alberta, especially from Sundre and Rocky Mountain House, would be like removing Canmore from Kananaskis', EB-780) and suggests adding the Stoney to a west-central riding (EB-782); Canmore-Kananaskis kept separate. Opposes interim Banff-Jasper placing Big Horn, O'Chiese and Sunchild away from Rocky (EB-780). Direction: does not say whether the Banff townsite is in or out.

quote: Cremona should be – it is not currently; it probably should have been caught in the last map – on the 22 side.
note: Wants Sundre and western Mountain View County (the 'highway 22 communities') with Rocky Mountain House rather than with the Highway 2 communities; per codebook partial-request rule this is O1. Says nothing about Crossfield, Irricana or Beiseker.

asks: Do not combine Edmonton-Glenora and Edmonton-Riverview; keep Brookside in Edmonton-Whitemud and add Mactaggart to it.
No change for Gold Bar; she is happy with the interim map's limited hybrids and asks the commission to account for Edmonton growth, perhaps with another seat.

Keep mid-sized cities as anchors of their own districts; consider not splitting Beaumont (keep it with Leduc or move part into Edmonton), listen to Enoch, and account for core Edmonton growth in districts already over average.

note: St. Albert and Morinville named only as an example of an edge-city hybrid that makes sense, and St. Albert as a city that fills a district (EB-791); rule 6, mention only.

asks: Keep Edmonton-Mill Woods to Mill Woods neighbourhoods: move Larkspur to Edmonton-Meadows, add a Mill Woods neighbourhood south of 23rd Avenue instead, and rename Edmonton-South East (perhaps Decoteau).
Keep Edmonton-Highlands-Norwood about as proposed (Spruce Avenue also acceptable); do not merge Edmonton-Glenora and Edmonton-Riverview; add another Edmonton seat.

Use a rural-urban hybrid model for southern Alberta: districts joining parts of Lethbridge with the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton, Cardston, Magrath, Raymond and Stirling, and Taber-Warner in a Lethbridge hybrid, so more than two MLAs represent Lethbridge; split the proposed Cardston-Taber-Warner along the Raymond-Stirling line.

quote: I think that a hybrid of Lethbridge with more MLAs representing that city but also representing the areas that surround that city would be an effective way of doing it.
note: Proposes a district with parts of Lethbridge, the Crowsnest Pass, Waterton, Cardston, Magrath, Raymond and Stirling, and Taber-Warner as 'part of a hybrid Lethbridge riding of its own' (EB-826); defends 'this quad hybrid model' when the Chair names it (EB-827), without confirming four seats. Direction, not exact.

asks: Keep the interim Edmonton-Whitemud (with Magrath and Mactaggart), add at least one more Edmonton seat, minimize hybrids at Edmonton's edges, and keep apportionment based on total population rather than eligible voters or turnout.
Keep Larkspur in Edmonton-Meadows so the Meadows Community League is not split, and consider an additional Edmonton seat.
